newsitem.title: USA: U.S. announces new Burma sanctions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. announces new Burma sanctions.

text.p: The United States announced new sanctions on Burma on Tuesday in the face of what it considers deepening political repression.
"President (Bill) Clinton has decided to impose a ban on new investment by Americans in Burma," Secretary of State Madeleine Albright told reporters at the State Department.
U.S. officials said the decision did not affect existing investments.

Albright said: "The decision is based on the president's judgment that the repression by the military authorities of the democratic opposition in Burma has deepened since enactment of the Cohen-Feinstein provisions this past September 30, and that a state of largescale repression exists."

Under that provision, named for the bill's congressional sponsors, the president was given authority to stiffen existing sanctions on the Southeast Asian state should he deem repression has increased.

The United States has halted direct financial assistance and blocked much international aid since the current military rulers, who call themselves the State Law and Order Restoration Council, took power in Burma in 1988.
